project.title: Integrated Early Support Programme for At-Risk Children
project.objective: Design and pilot a coordinated school-community support programme for at-risk children to improve wellbeing, safety, and readiness for later schooling.
deliverables: Shared early identification and referral protocol between school and social services
Standardised classroom support routines for at-risk children
Staff training session plan and materials
Monitoring and reporting template for child progress and incidents
constraints: Pilot must run within one school term with minimal disruption to classes
All procedures must comply with child safeguarding and data protection policies
Documentation must be understandable for both education and social care staff
Limited availability for home visits outside core working hours
Any new routines must fit existing kindergarten school procedures

risks.risk: Low family engagement with the new support programme.
risks.mitigation: Create clear, simple information materials and flexible contact options; involve parents early in planning.

risks.risk: Teachers and assistants feel overloaded by additional routines.
risks.mitigation: Co-design routines with staff, keep checklists short, and align with existing classroom practices.

risks.risk: Information sharing between school and social services breaches confidentiality rules.
risks.mitigation: Define strict consent and data-sharing rules and include them in the referral protocol and training.

risks.risk: Inconsistent application of the protocol across different classes or social workers.
risks.mitigation: Provide a simple checklist, brief training, and regular short check-ins during the pilot.

themes.why_relevant: Core to both school and social work roles; must be consistent across settings.

themes.theme: Early identification of learning and wellbeing difficulties
themes.why_relevant: Timely support depends on spotting signs early in class and at home.
Programme success relies on smooth coordination between education and social services.
Parents and guardians must understand and support the new programme.
New routines must fit into busy school days and social work schedules.

backlog.task: Map current school and social work procedures for identifying and referring at-risk children
definition_of_done: Existing school procedures documented in a shared document
Existing social services referral steps documented
Overlaps and gaps between procedures listed
Document reviewed by one community social worker and one early years teaching assistant

backlog.task: Draft a joint early identification and referral protocol for at-risk children
definition_of_done: Draft protocol includes roles, steps, and consent requirements
Protocol aligns with safeguarding and data protection rules
Draft shared with early years teaching assistants and social workers for comments
Feedback incorporated into a second draft

backlog.task: Design classroom observation checklist for early signs of learning or wellbeing difficulties
definition_of_done: Checklist covers behaviour, learning, and safety indicators
Checklist can be completed within 5 minutes per child
Reviewed and approved by a social worker for relevance
Pilot version ready for use in two classes

backlog.task: Create a simple family engagement script and leaflet explaining the programme
definition_of_done: Script for initial parent conversations drafted
Leaflet text written in clear, non-technical language
Early years teaching assistants confirm it fits school communication style
Materials checked for compliance with organisational guidelines

backlog.task: Define criteria and schedule for home visits or community follow-up
definition_of_done: Clear criteria for when a home visit is recommended
Standard steps for planning and documenting visits listed
Constraints on visit times and safety procedures included
Shared with school leadership for awareness

backlog.task: Develop standardised classroom support routines for identified at-risk children
definition_of_done: List of 5–8 practical support strategies agreed
Routines align with curriculum objectives and classroom management rules
Social worker confirms routines support social-emotional needs
Routines documented in a short guideline

backlog.task: Prepare a short training session for school and social work staff on the new protocol
definition_of_done: Training objectives and agenda defined
Slides or handouts drafted
Includes case examples from both school and community contexts
Session plan reviewed by a community social worker and an early years teaching assistant

backlog.task: Create a shared monitoring and reporting template for child progress and incidents
definition_of_done: Template includes wellbeing, learning, and safety sections
Fields are clear for both school and social work staff
Data protection requirements reflected in fields and storage notes
Template tested with at least one sample case

backlog.task: Plan the pilot schedule and select participating classes and families
definition_of_done: Two to three classes identified for the pilot
Indicative number of children and families listed
Timeline for rollout agreed with school leadership
Risks and constraints for the pilot documented

backlog.task: Define quick feedback loop for staff during the pilot
definition_of_done: Simple method for staff to share issues and suggestions agreed
Frequency of check-ins set (e.g. weekly)
Responsibilities for collecting and summarising feedback assigned
Process documented in the project guideline

backlog.task: Align the programme with existing kindergarten school procedures and organisational guidelines
definition_of_done: Key school procedures and organisational guidelines reviewed
Any conflicts or overlaps with the new programme identified
Adjustments proposed and documented
School leadership sign-off recorded

backlog.task: Define indicators to evaluate the pilot's impact on child wellbeing and safety
definition_of_done: 3–5 simple indicators agreed (e.g. incidents, attendance, observed wellbeing)
Data sources and collection frequency defined
Responsibilities for recording and reviewing data assigned
Indicators added to the monitoring template

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on current procedures and confirm scope of the integrated support programme.
threads_plan.trigger: Kickoff message asking everyone to share how they currently identify and refer at-risk children.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Agree on the final scope of the pilot (number of classes and types of cases included).
Confirm ownership for completing the current procedures mapping document.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Review and finalise the early identification and referral protocol and observation checklist.
threads_plan.trigger: Community social worker posts draft protocol and asks for school-side feedback.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the early identification and referral protocol for pilot use.
Agree on the final version of the classroom observation checklist and how often it is used.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Define classroom support routines and align them with school procedures and workload.
threads_plan.trigger: Early years teaching assistant shares draft support routines and asks if they are realistic.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Select the set of classroom support strategies to include in the guideline.
Decide how support routines will be documented and stored for staff access.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Agree on family engagement approach and home visit criteria.
threads_plan.trigger: Social worker posts the draft family engagement script and home visit criteria for comments.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the family engagement script and leaflet wording.
Confirm criteria and safety rules for home visits and community follow-up.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Lock in monitoring indicators, reporting template, and pilot start date.
threads_plan.trigger: Community social worker shares the monitoring template and proposed indicators.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Reconfirm pilot scope and start date based on readiness of materials.
Reconfirm protocol approval after any final tweaks from monitoring needs.

channel_rituals: Daily short async check-in each morning on any urgent child safety or wellbeing concerns.
Twice-weekly async standup focusing on progress against pilot tasks and blockers.
Weekly summary post capturing decisions, updated documents, and next steps.
End-of-pilot async retrospective thread to capture lessons learned and improvement ideas.
